models_evaluated: Bayesian Gaussian Process Classifier (ARD Matérn 2.5 kernel)

links.outcome: Performance drop from internal development population to external UK Biobank breast cancer cohort
links.effect: Balanced accuracy fell from 0.987 internally to 0.835 externally; specificity fell from 0.997 to 0.856 while sensitivity stayed at 0.814 (vs 0.978). Non-risk ECGs with InflectionPoint ≥4.5 rose from 7.3% to 15.1%.
links.quote: Externally, Balanced Accuracy was 0.835, sensitivity 0.814 and specificity 0.856.

links.outcome: Generalization of a TdP risk model applied without retraining to a new population
links.effect: Applied without retraining, balanced accuracy dropped from 0.987 (internal) to 0.835 (external); specificity fell most (0.997 to 0.856).
links.quote: Internally, Balanced Accuracy was 0.987, sensitivity 0.978 and specificity 0.997.

unlisted_practices: Decomposing predictive uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components to diagnose causes of errors under population shift
Using explainability analyses (ARD length-scales, permutation importance, SHAP) to identify features driving performance loss externally

screen.reason: The study conducts external validation and uncertainty quantification/explainability analysis of an ECG-based machine learning risk prediction model across population shifts (from healthy volunteers to a clinical breast cancer cohort). It does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
